thread.title: Morning Movers: Apple Lifts Tech While Trade Hits the Dow

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Morning Movers: Apple Lifts Tech While Trade Hits the Dow
text:
By Teresa Rivas Aug. 1, 2018 9:28 a.m. ET Not Again. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was falling before the open on fresh trade war worries . Apple (AAPL) is rising after its earnings , boosting its suppliers and tech stocks in general. Then of course we'll hear from the Federal Reserve this afternoon, although no rate hike is expected today.
In today's Morning Movers , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...review Apple (AAPL) earnings;
•...prepare for the Federal Reserve's statement this afternoon;
•....and discuss tariffs once again.
Three Times the Fun
Sales of iPhones are floating tech stocks higher this morning, although there are plenty of other factors moving the market.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 0.1% in early trading as trade war escalation seems once again to be on the table; while S&P 500 futures clinging to gains of less than 0.1%. The Nasdaq Composite is up 0.3%, helped by Apple (AAPL) earnings.
The tech giant's earnings are one of a trio of big stories today. Apple's rise is a welcome change from the big disappointments from Facebook (FB) and Netflix (NFLX), and it means that more FAANG stocks than not have climbed after reporting earnings, despite social media's high-profile struggles. Or as GBH Insights' Daniel Ives writes, "after the heartburn seen from the earnings disappointments across tech bellwethers such as Facebook and Netflix over the last few weeks, Apple gave the Street and tech investors finally some good news with a clean June headline beat and stronger than expected outlook."
Apple's upbeat quarter is part of a broader pattern, writes Credit Suisse's Jonathan Golub , as the U.S. earnings growth is outpacing the rest of the world even without tax benefits, and surpassing expectations even as international results disappoint.
Pre-Apple results, tech had underperformed the broader market by 3.8% following Facebook's release. While Apple may help alleviate worries about the sector, investors will likely remain on alert for cracks in the FAANG story.
If nothing else, "perhaps this recent pullback [in tech] will create more realistic expectations for these stocks going forward," writes Shannon Saccocia, CIO of Boston Private . Looking ahead, she believes that the market will continue to distinguish between the haves and have-nots, those that can provide compelling products and experiences and those that are slipping. "Not all technology stocks are created alike, and as we move forward through the back half of the year, this differentiation in performance amongst the group is likely to persist."
With tech accounting for such a big part of the S&P 500, investors have been understandably nervous about whether or not the recent downturn heralded a broader slowdown for the market. Certainly, there are other ways for markets to notch highs without tech , but a tech slump would of course make it harder.
With an aging bull market, investors may be wary of any hint of a slump, and some even see another correction coming on par with February's selloff. Not everyone is preparing for the worst, however. Smead Capital's Bill Smead argues that the bull market isn't as old as many investors think: Sure, this recovery is one of the longest on record, but it's also a very "anemic" recovery given the magnitude of the Great Recession. "We would argue that this recovery really started two years ago when home building began to positively impact economic growth. Normally, housing drives the early stages of an economic recovery due to lower interest rates. Currently, new home inventory is running 25-35% below historical norms, based on available inventory versus outstanding households."
Illustration: Bloomberg News Speaking of interest rates, that will be another big story of the day as we wait to hear from the Federal Reserve this afternoon. Recall that in June the central bank raised rates and signaled we could expect two more hikes this year, although one isn't expected today.
Osterweis Capital Management’s Carl Kaufman notes that past recessions have often be presaged by the fed-funds rate approaching the nominal gross domestic product growth rate, and we are still comfortably far from that happening. “If we had to draw one conclusion from this, it would be that we are still 100-150 basis points (1.0%-1.5%) below where we should start to worry that short-term interest rates are a concern for economic growth.”
But wait, you didn't forget about the trade war did you? That's the third big story today. Some in the administration are pushing the president to crank the heat up on China yet again as Washington and Beijing prepare to sit down to talk. Tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese imports are still on the table, but now the levy in question should be pushed as high as 25%, from the original 10%, some advisors are urging. This comes as Congress takes aim at China as well, with a new defense bill.
While Washington appears set on punishing China, Silicon Valley may be feeling more conciliatory. The Intercept reports today that Alphabet (GOOGL) is planning to launch a censored version of its search engine in China, marking the first time in nearly a decade Chinese internet users will be able to Google something.
Tech was seen as one of the few quasi-safe havens when the trade war worries were weighing on the market in recent months. Google, of course, is likely bowing to Chinese pressure with an eye to future growth. But concessions may make it unpopular if Washington ever gets around to the simmering threat of breaking up big tech companies.
Morning Movers
Earnings & News
Akamai Technologies (AKAM) is down 5.2% to $71.38 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The bandwidth provider earned 83 cents a share on revenue of $663 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 80 cents on revenue of $661.13 million.
Illustration: Apple Inc. Apple (AAPL) is up 4.4% to $198.63 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The tech giant earned $2.34 a share on revenue of $53.3 billion. Analysts expected earnings of $2.18 a share on revenue of $52.43 billion. For the fourth quarter, it expects revenue of $60 billion to $62 billion, compared with the $59.4 billion consensus estimate.
Cheesecake Factory (CAKE) is down 9.9% to $50.50 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The restaurant chain earned 65 cents a share on revenue of $593.2 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 81 cents on revenue of $592.4 million.
Devon Energy (DVN) is down 4.5% to $43 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The energy firm earned 34 cents a share, compared with the 38 cent consensus estimate.
Garmin (GRMN) is up 3% to $64.32 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The fitness technology firm earned 99 cents a share on revenue of $894.5 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 87 cents on revenue of $844.76 million. For the full year, it sees EPS of $3.30, compared with the $3.13 consensus estimate.
Humana (HUM) is up 1.5% to $319 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The health insurer earned $3.96 a share, above the $3.78 consensus. For the full year, it sees EPS of $14.15, up from $13.70 to $14.10, and compared with the $13.98 consensus estimate.
McDermott International (MDR) is up 1.7% to $18.31 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The construction and engineering firm earned 29 cents a share on revenue of $1.74 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 26 cents on revenue of $1.98 billion.
Pandora (P) is up 12.3% to $7.60 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The streaming music service lost 15 cents a share on revenue of $384.8 million. Analysts were looking for a 17-cent loss on revenue of $372.52 million.
Sprint (S) is up 2% to $5.54 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The wireless carrier earned 4 cents a share on revenue of $8.13 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of a penny on revenue of $8.05 billion.
Whiting Petroleum (WLL) is down 3.7% to $47.80 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The oil and gas producer earned 62 cents a share on revenue of $526.4 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 64 cents a share on revenue of $505.32 million.
Upgrades & Downgrades
AutoZone (AZO) is up 0.6% to $709.48 after Deutsche Bank upgraded it to Buy.
Canada Goose (GOOS) is down 3.9% to $55.21 after Robert W. Baird downgraded it to Neutral.
Papa John's International (PZZA) is up 3.2% to $43.30 after Jefferies upgraded it to Buy.
Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT) is up 4.3% to $121.25 after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to Overweight.
Tableau Software (DATA) is up 1.9% to $105.05 after Deutsche Bank upgraded it to Buy.
